solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Highly-paid actor in article with Hudson?

parts.note: the definite article is one of the grammar articles
Rock Hudson was a Hollywood film star; Hudson is also this puzzle's setter

explanation.surface: The setter wonders whether a well-paid film star appears in a piece written by Hudson himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Hudson is the setter's pseudonym, so the clue looks like a joke about the setter; it is Rock Hudson's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwayne Johnson, the wrestler turned film star and one of Hollywood's best-paid performers, goes by this stage name.

clue.text: Pressure on Hants opener without runs mounting — lots of movement through the air here

definitions.text: lots of movement through the air here

parts.note: being under heat means being under pressure

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, as an opening batsman goes in first
in a down clue, mounting means the letters climb, read from the bottom up

parts.note: w/o is the written shorthand for without
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket report: pressure on Hampshire's opening batsman, who is failing to score as the attack builds.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county with a cricket team. 'mounting' turns WO plus R into ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: London's main airport sees vast numbers of flights taking off and landing, so huge air traffic passes through it.

clue.text: Bad hombre guzzling over a bottle

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing something whole, so one part takes in the other
something bad is spoiled or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Spanish word for man, used here only for its letters
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A villainous man in a Western swigging from a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges HOMBRE to REHOBM, which 'guzzling' wraps round O and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wine bottle holding about six standard bottles is named after a biblical king of Judah.

clue.text: Native American, similar to Caligula and his consul

parts.note: the Roman emperor Caligula was reputedly insane, so like him is mad
Caligula is said to have planned to make his horse Incitatus a consul

explanation.surface: A historical comparison likening someone to Caligula and the official who served him.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'consul' is the famous tale of Caligula intending to appoint his favourite horse to the consulship.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lakota war leader who fought at the Little Bighorn in 1876 bore this name.

clue.text: Scalped head in bygone days

indicators.note: scalping removes the top of the head, so the word for head loses its top letter

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A grim frontier image of a scalped head from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is everyday British slang for head; in a down clue its top is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly or at one time, as in a story about the past: a straightforward synonym for long ago.

clue.text: Phone card flipping low — that's a blow

parts.note: a SIM card goes in a mobile phone

indicators.note: flipping turns the cattle sound over so it reads backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Someone's mobile card turns out flipping useless, and what a blow that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a British mild oath; it reverses MOO to OOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Blow here is a wind: a hot, dry, dusty desert wind of Arabia and North Africa.

clue.text: Stops lessons

definitions.meaning: full stops, the punctuation marks Americans call by this name
school timetable slots, each class session of the day

explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is called by this name in American usage, and a school day is divided into timetabled class sessions with the same name.

clue.text: In Paris, my uncle loses second new lens

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to drop the second of the two Ns in the French words

parts.note: mon oncle is French for my uncle

explanation.surface: A French uncle mislays his spare lens.
explanation.walkthrough: Mon Oncle is also a Jacques Tati film, which adds colour to the French surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A single eyeglass worn in one eye socket is a lone corrective lens.

clue.text: Hit back, punching a notorious Roman baddie

indicators.note: punching means driving into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Nero, the emperor said to have fiddled while Rome burned

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word Hit from right to left

explanation.surface: A fight scene: someone hits back, punching a notorious Roman villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit back' reads as retaliation, but 'back' is the reversal signal, and 'punching' puts the reversed letters just after the N of the Roman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist lacking heroic virtues is close kin to a villain; the clue treats the flawed lead as a bad guy.

clue.text: Connery's Arab citadel where the vodka martinis aren't free?

definitions.text: where the vodka martinis aren't free?

indicators.note: Sean Connery famously slurred his s sounds into sh, so this is his way of saying the word

parts.note: a casbah is the walled citadel of a North African city

explanation.surface: James Bond, as played by Connery, in a Moroccan fortress ordering martinis he must pay for.
explanation.walkthrough: Connery's Bond drank vodka martinis; his slushy 's' turns the citadel into the paid bar.
explanation.definitionFit: At an event with a pay-as-you-go bar, guests buy their own drinks rather than having them laid on.

clue.text: Apache helicopter paratroops' departure call?

definitions.meaning: a famous Apache leader who resisted US forces in the 1880s
the cry American paratroopers traditionally shout as they jump out

explanation.walkthrough: The Apache is also a US attack helicopter, which welds the two halves into one military picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache war leader's name became the shout made by US airborne troops as they leap from the aircraft.

clue.text: 1 soldier, British (a lieutenant) upset regiment

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 1 across, a nickname for the place

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: the RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: A list of military personnel at odds with the regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' points to the answer at 1 across, the famous nickname of this British territory; 'upset' reverses RA.
explanation.definitionFit: This British Overseas Territory at the tip of Spain is known by the nickname at 1 across, after its great limestone promontory.

clue.text: Lead with clubs; partner's overweight

indicators.note: lead with says this letter comes at the front of the word

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
a hubby is a husband, a marriage partner; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Bridge table talk: lead a club, because partner holds too many cards in that suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump or podgy: a casual synonym for carrying extra body weight.

clue.text: Mo — bald head — runs weekly

indicators.note: letters that run, like dye, lose their order and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bald man called Mo goes jogging once a week.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare formal adjective comes from the Greek for a group of seven, so it describes something happening every seven days.

clue.text: Legside boundaries keeping everyone in a defensive position

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a ball reaching the boundary along the ground scores four, so boundaries are fours
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: boundaries hit through the leg side force a defensive field setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side, the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs, is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Crouching on hands and knees is a protective posture, curled and low to the ground.

clue.text: The first spreadsheet entry goes here, pop

definitions.text: The first spreadsheet entry goes here
definitions.meaning: a spreadsheet starts at cell A1, in the column lettered A
pop is a fizzy soft drink

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as COL A, the abbreviation for the spreadsheet column lettered A.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy soft drink, typically brown and sweet, is the classic example of soda pop.

clue.text: Madame la Reine originally mixing confiture

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the start, the opening letter of Reine

explanation.surface: A French queen stirring a pot of jam in the royal kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Confiture is a French word for preserves; this citrus preserve made with bitter oranges is a kind of it.

clue.text: Genius's curt order for beer at the Oktoberfest?

definitions.meaning: a genius, a brilliant scientist; the 's stands for is

definitions.text: curt order for beer at the Oktoberfest?
definitions.meaning: in German ein is one and a stein is a beer mug, so this is a two-word request for one mug

explanation.definitionFit: The physicist behind relativity is the byword for brilliance, used of any clever person.

clue.text: Legless chum, annoyed, bottles German barman

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the letters are contained within these words

explanation.surface: A drunk friend, irritated, keeps the German behind the bar in bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barman' is not a bartender but a composer, a man who writes bars of music; 'Legless' is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert, the Romantic composer from Saxony, wrote music measured in bars, so he is a maker of bars.

clue.text: Compere almost crushing supporter in bear-hug?

indicators.note: crushing means squeezing round, so one piece encloses the other
almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an emcee, or MC, is a compere or host
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A show host squeezes a fan in a crushing bear-hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a fan of the host, but it is an item of underwear; 'almost' drops the final letter of the host's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight hug with both arms around someone is a strong form of a clasp or hold.

clue.text: When mate's expected on board?

parts.note: mate suggests a ship's officer coming aboard, but it is checkmate on a chessboard, which arrives in the closing phase

explanation.surface: A sailor asks when the first mate will be coming aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stage of a chess game, when few pieces remain and checkmate is near.

clue.text: Maeve's exposed Irish island

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the surname loses its outer letters

parts.note: Maeve Binchy was a popular Irish novelist

explanation.surface: An Irish island laid bare in a novel by Maeve Binchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Maeve Binchy, the bestselling Irish author, supplies her surname, which 'exposed' strips of its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish and Scottish place names this word means an islet, and there is an Inch Island in Donegal.

clue.text: Enormous tunnel blown up with ammo

indicators.note: blown up means exploded, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge tunnel destroyed with explosives, as in a war film.
explanation.definitionFit: Something massive in scale or importance, like a huge public structure, is gigantic.

clue.text: Teacher married Daisy

parts.note: the aster is a flower of the daisy family

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher has wed a woman called Daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a male schoolteacher, and the shorter title is an old term for one.

clue.text: It might be part of green fee, touring Southern Corfu on vacation

definitions.text: It might be part of green

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the outer word goes round the inner pieces

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so Corfu loses its inside letters and keeps only its ends

explanation.surface: Golfers paying the green fee while on holiday touring southern Corfu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' is a golf green, not the colour, and 'green fee' is what golfers pay.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine-leaved grass is commonly sown on golf greens and lawns, so it forms part of one.

clue.text: Record drift in Scripture, English and arithmetic?

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the British school subject once called Scripture
the drift of an argument is its gist
arithmetic is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: A school report noting the general drift in Scripture, English and maths lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, Religious Education, is a British school subject; the 'three Rs' are basic schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: An official list or log, such as a school attendance roll, is a written record.

clue.text: What about about about a head?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: eh is a questioning what?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A puzzled question repeating the word about, as if someone is stuck on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 'about' has a different job: around, circa, and turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: Per person, as in costing a pound apiece: a price for every individual.

clue.text: Retiring Greek character garlanded with wild send-off

indicators.note: garlanded with means wreathed around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: feral means wild, as of an untamed animal

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A shy Greek figure decked in flowers at a riotous farewell party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like a description of a shy person; it reverses NU to UN.
explanation.definitionFit: A send-off is a farewell ceremony, and the last farewell is the ceremony for the dead.

clue.text: Force to accept two thousand in trade

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to coerce is to force
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them are MM

explanation.surface: Pressure to take a two-thousand payment in a business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying and selling on a large scale is a synonym for business dealing.

clue.text: Stupid, like current 9?

parts.note: as means like
I is the physics symbol for electric current
the numeral 9 written out as a word

explanation.surface: Asking whether a figure in a puzzle is as silly as entry 9.
explanation.walkthrough: The '9' looks like a pointer to 9 across; it is just the number, spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish or silly: a synonym from the Latin for donkey-like.
